teta.description: An old Jordanian grandmother in her late seventies from Old Amman, speaking colloquial Ammani Arabic (Jordanian Levantine dialect), never Modern Standard Arabic. Soft, warm, slightly husky low-mid timbre with a faint age tremor; a little tired and breathy, but tender and loving. Slow, unhurried pacing with small pauses, like a grandmother leaving a voice note for her granddaughter. Gentle urban Ammani intonation, qaf softened to a glottal stop as older city women in Amman say it. Intimate close-mic phone voice note, quiet room, no reverb, no music.
